results.title: Built-In Car Entertainment Systems: Are They Worth the Money?
results.content:
Car entertainment systems (also called rear-seat entertainment systems) consist of screens mounted on the back of front-seat headrests or suspended from the ceiling of the car. They are designed to keep passengers – especially children – entertained when traveling. They can come with one or two screens, a DVD or Blu-ray player (mostly in older systems), HDMI ports, and streaming apps such as Netflix and YouTube. Depending on the automaker, some rear-seat entertainment systems let users plug in [...] Convenience:Rear-seat entertainment systems provide convenience that makes long trips more bearable for everyone in the vehicle. Passengers don’t need to rely on personal devices or juggle multiple tablets and chargers, because everything they need is built into the car. Both kids and adult riders can settle in with movies, TV shows, music, or games. Having something to watch, listen to, or play transforms travel time into personal downtime and helps pass the miles. [...] Aftermarket: Aftermarket rear-seat entertainment systems are typically less expensive than factory-installed options. However, the system may be less integrated with your vehicle’s infotainment system and may not match the interior of your car. Aftermarket back-seat entertainment systems can range from a simple screen that attaches to the back seat to a complex, professionally designed installation that is custom-tailored for your vehicle.

results.content:
Rear Seat EntertainmentIf you have an aftermarket multimedia receiver installed in your dash, then you can probably use that to play movies for rear-seat passengers. Your passengers will still need monitors in the rear, since it’s illegal in most states and provinces to have a video entertainment system playing within view of the driver. [...] ## Headrest Monitor Solutions

Rear Seat EntertainmentHeadrest monitor solutions are the same as the screens in an airplane. For the rear-seat passengers, the screens are on the back of the driver and passenger headrests. There are two options for headrest screens: a display installed in most factory headrests, or a replacement headrest unit. [...] A few companies make monitor systems that attach to the rear of a center console or strap to the seat in front of you. While these solutions don’t integrated with the vehicle as cleanly, they do offer entertainment – and that’s what matters.

If there is no dedicated rear-seat entertainment solution for your vehicle, don’t despair. Many mobile electronics retailers can create something for you from scratch. A custom tablet mount for the seat or center console isn’t a problem for most of them.
